protocol: max AP-ROP probability per session, threshold 0.5 fixed a priori; Ostrava sessions keyed by device+serie from the filename, non-Ostrava AP-ROP grouped per patient (no session structure exists there). Same 119 units both seeds.
fp_note: normal-session FP here uses ALL normal units incl. patient-fallback ones (19/1639 = 1.16%). The earlier committed 0.25% used Ostrava-keyed normal sessions only. PIN ONE DEFINITION IN THE PAPER and state it; both are honest, they are different denominators.

frames_without_the_appearance.what: Fraction of AP-ROP-LABELLED frames the model scores p_arop<0.1 — 'the label is carried, the appearance is absent'. Pooled out-of-fold over the 5 structured folds (seed 42).
frames_without_the_appearance.reading: This is the finding's internal control. Ostrava stamps one diagnosis code on every frame of an examination session, and 70% of its AP-ROP frames score below 0.1. The other sources label 1-2 frames per infant, and only 10% do. Same model, same class, 7x the rate exactly where the labelling is per-session - so the frames are not mysteriously hard, they are mislabelled by inheritance.
frames_without_the_appearance.supersedes: session_level_arop.json's median_frac_frames_below_p0.1_in_arop_sessions = 0.4706, which was computed on an EARLIER prediction set (its fold-0 image recall is 0.311 vs the canonical 0.212) and on fold 0 alone. Do not quote the 47%.
